questions.stem: A shopkeeper marks an article \(25\%\) above the cost price and allows a discount of \(10\%\). If the cost price is Rs. \(800\), what is the profit percentage?
questions.keySolution:
Cost price = Rs. \(800\)
Marked price = \(800 + 25\% \text{ of } 800 = 800 + 200 = Rs. 1000\)
Discount = \(10\% \text{ of } 1000 = Rs. 100\)
Selling price = \(1000 - 100 = Rs. 900\)
Profit = \(900 - 800 = Rs. 100\)
Profit percentage = \(\frac{100}{800} \times 100 = 12.5\%\)

questions.stem: Two successive discounts of \(20\%\) and \(15\%\) are equivalent to a single discount of:
questions.keySolution:
For two successive discounts of \(a\%\) and \(b\%\):
Single equivalent discount = \(a + b - \frac{ab}{100}\)
Here, \(a = 20, b = 15\)
Single discount = \(20 + 15 - \frac{20 \times 15}{100} = 35 - 3 = 32\%\)

questions.stem: A dealer offers \(10\%\) discount on marked price and still makes \(25\%\) profit. If the cost price is Rs. \(720\), find the marked price:
questions.keySolution:
Cost price = Rs. \(720\)
Profit = \(25\%\), so selling price = \(720 \times 1.25 = Rs. 900\)
Let marked price = \(x\)
After \(10\%\) discount: \(x \times 0.9 = 900\)
Therefore, \(x = \frac{900}{0.9} = Rs. 1000\)

questions.stem: The difference between two selling prices of an article at profits of \(20\%\) and \(25\%\) is Rs. \(50\). The cost price of the article is:
questions.keySolution:
Let cost price = \(C\)
Selling price at \(20\%\) profit = \(1.2C\)
Selling price at \(25\%\) profit = \(1.25C\)
Difference = \(1.25C - 1.2C = 0.05C = 50\)
Therefore, \(C = \frac{50}{0.05} = Rs. 1000\)

questions.stem: A shopkeeper allows \(15\%\) discount on marked price and still gains \(19\%\). If the gain is Rs. \(171\), find the cost price:
questions.keySolution:
Let cost price = \(C\)
Gain = \(19\% \text{ of } C = 0.19C = 171\)
Therefore, \(C = \frac{171}{0.19} = Rs. 900\)

questions.stem: After giving \(12\%\) discount on an article, a trader gains \(10\%\). If he gives \(15\%\) discount, his gain percent will be:
questions.keySolution:
Let cost price = \(100\) and marked price = \(M\)
After \(12\%\) discount with \(10\%\) gain:
\(0.88M = 110\), so \(M = 125\)
With \(15\%\) discount: Selling price = \(0.85 \times 125 = 106.25\)
Gain = \(106.25 - 100 = 6.25\%\)

questions.stem: A retailer buys goods worth Rs. \(4500\) and sells them at \(20\%\) discount on marked price. If he marks the goods at \(50\%\) above cost price, his profit percentage is:
questions.keySolution:
Cost price = Rs. \(4500\)
Marked price = \(4500 \times 1.5 = Rs. 6750\)
Selling price after \(20\%\) discount = \(6750 \times 0.8 = Rs. 5400\)
Profit = \(5400 - 4500 = Rs. 900\)
Profit percentage = \(\frac{900}{4500} \times 100 = 20\%\)

questions.stem: The marked price of an article is \(30\%\) more than its cost price. If \(12\%\) discount is allowed, the gain percent is:
questions.keySolution:
Let cost price = \(100\)
Marked price = \(130\)
Selling price after \(12\%\) discount = \(130 \times 0.88 = 114.4\)
Gain = \(114.4 - 100 = 14.4\%\)

questions.stem: A man buys an article for Rs. \(1200\) and marks it \(40\%\) above cost price. He sells it at \(25\%\) discount. His gain or loss percent is:
questions.keySolution:
Cost price = Rs. \(1200\)
Marked price = \(1200 \times 1.4 = Rs. 1680\)
Selling price = \(1680 \times 0.75 = Rs. 1260\)
Gain = \(1260 - 1200 = Rs. 60\)
Gain percent = \(\frac{60}{1200} \times 100 = 5\%\)

questions.stem: Three successive discounts of \(10\%\), \(20\%\) and \(30\%\) are equivalent to a single discount of:
questions.keySolution:
After \(10\%\) discount: \(90\%\) remains
After \(20\%\) discount on remaining: \(90\% \times 80\% = 72\%\)
After \(30\%\) discount on remaining: \(72\% \times 70\% = 50.4\%\)
Single discount = \(100\% - 50.4\% = 49.6\%\)

questions.stem: A dealer sells an article at \(5\%\) loss. Had he sold it for Rs. \(104\) more, he would have gained \(8\%\). The cost price is:
questions.keySolution:
Let cost price = \(C\)
Selling price at \(5\%\) loss = \(0.95C\)
Selling price at \(8\%\) gain = \(1.08C\)
Difference = \(1.08C - 0.95C = 0.13C = 104\)
Therefore, \(C = \frac{104}{0.13} = Rs. 800\)

questions.stem: If selling price is \(96\%\) of marked price and the profit is \(20\%\), then the marked price is what percent more than cost price?
questions.keySolution:
Let cost price = \(100\)
Profit = \(20\%\), so selling price = \(120\)
Selling price = \(96\%\) of marked price
So \(120 = 0.96 \times \text{MP}\)
Marked price = \(\frac{120}{0.96} = 125\)
Marked price is \(25\%\) more than cost price

questions.stem: If the discount allowed on an article is \(20\%\) of its marked price and the profit earned is \(25\%\) of its cost price, what is the ratio of cost price to marked price?
questions.keySolution:
Let cost price = \(C\) and marked price = \(M\)
Discount = \(20\%\) of \(M = 0.2M\)
Selling price = \(M - 0.2M = 0.8M\)
Profit = \(25\%\) of \(C\), so selling price = \(1.25C\)
Therefore, \(0.8M = 1.25C\)
\(\frac{C}{M} = \frac{0.8}{1.25} = \frac{4}{5}\)

questions.stem: The cost price of \(20\) articles is equal to selling price of \(16\) articles. Find the profit percent:
questions.keySolution:
Let cost price of each article = \(C\)
Cost price of \(20\) articles = \(20C\)
This equals selling price of \(16\) articles
Selling price of each article = \(\frac{20C}{16} = \frac{5C}{4} = 1.25C\)
Profit per article = \(1.25C - C = 0.25C\)
Profit percent = \(\frac{0.25C}{C} \times 100 = 25\%\)

questions.stem: A trader allows a discount of \(15\%\) on marked price. How much percent above the cost price must he mark his goods to make a profit of \(19\%\)?
questions.keySolution:
Let cost price = \(100\)
Desired selling price for \(19\%\) profit = \(119\)
Let marked price = \(M\)
After \(15\%\) discount: \(0.85M = 119\)
Therefore, \(M = \frac{119}{0.85} = 140\)
Marked price is \(40\%\) above cost price

questions.stem: What single discount is equivalent to two successive discounts of \(25\%\) and \(8\%\)?
questions.keySolution:
Single equivalent discount = \(25 + 8 - \frac{25 \times 8}{100}\)
= \(33 - 2 = 31\%\)

questions.stem: A watch was sold at a profit of \(12\%\). If it had been sold for Rs. \(33\) less, there would have been a loss of \(8\%\). What is the cost price?
questions.keySolution:
Let cost price = \(C\)
Selling price at \(12\%\) profit = \(1.12C\)
Selling price at \(8\%\) loss = \(0.92C\)
Difference = \(1.12C - 0.92C = 0.2C = 33\)
Therefore, \(C = \frac{33}{0.2} = Rs. 165\)

questions.stem: The marked price of a book is Rs. \(500\). The shopkeeper allows successive discounts of \(10\%\), \(15\%\) and \(8\%\). The selling price is:
questions.keySolution:
After \(10\%\) discount: \(500 \times 0.9 = 450\)
After \(15\%\) discount: \(450 \times 0.85 = 382.5\)
After \(8\%\) discount: \(382.5 \times 0.92 = 351.9 ≈ Rs. 351\)

questions.stem: An article is listed at Rs. \(900\). A customer gets successive discounts of \(20\%\) and \(10\%\). He pays:
questions.keySolution:
After \(20\%\) discount: \(900 \times 0.8 = Rs. 720\)
After \(10\%\) discount: \(720 \times 0.9 = Rs. 648\)

questions.stem: A dealer marks his goods at such a price that after allowing a discount of \(25\%\), he still gains \(50\%\). If the cost price is Rs. \(1800\), the marked price is:
questions.keySolution:
Cost price = Rs. \(1800\)
Selling price at \(50\%\) gain = \(1800 \times 1.5 = Rs. 2700\)
Let marked price = \(M\)
After \(25\%\) discount: \(0.75M = 2700\)
Therefore, \(M = \frac{2700}{0.75} = Rs. 3600\)

questions.stem: A manufacturer sells goods to a wholesaler at \(10\%\) profit. The wholesaler sells to retailer at \(20\%\) profit. The retailer sells to customer at \(25\%\) profit. If customer pays Rs. \(1650\), find manufacturer's cost price:
questions.keySolution:
Working backwards from customer price:
Retailer's cost price = \(\frac{1650}{1.25} = Rs. 1320\)
Wholesaler's cost price = \(\frac{1320}{1.20} = Rs. 1100\)
Manufacturer's cost price = \(\frac{1100}{1.10} = Rs. 1000\)

questions.stem: If the selling price of \(15\) articles equals the cost price of \(20\) articles, then the gain percent is:
questions.keySolution:
Let cost price of each article = \(C\)
Cost price of \(20\) articles = \(20C\)
This equals selling price of \(15\) articles
Selling price of each article = \(\frac{20C}{15} = \frac{4C}{3}\)
Gain per article = \(\frac{4C}{3} - C = \frac{C}{3}\)
Gain percent = \(\frac{C/3}{C} \times 100 = 33\frac{1}{3}\%\)

questions.stem: A person sells his goods at cost price but uses a weight of \(900\)g instead of \(1\)kg. His gain percent is:
questions.keySolution:
Cost of \(1000\)g = Selling price of \(900\)g
Effective cost price of \(900\)g = \(\frac{900}{1000} \times \text{actual cost}\)
Gain = Selling price - Cost price = \(1 - 0.9 = 0.1\) units
Gain percent = \(\frac{0.1}{0.9} \times 100 = \frac{100}{9} = 11\frac{1}{9}\%\)
